questions.q: Simplify: $96 \div 4 \text{ of } 6 + 5 \times 8 \div 10 - 3$
questions.solution: 'of' is solved before $\div$: $4 \text{ of } 6 = 24$, so $96 \div 24 = 4$. Next $5 \times 8 \div 10 = 4$. Value $= 4 + 4 - 3 = 5$.
questions.shortcut: Read 'of' as a bracketed multiplication: $96 \div (4 \times 6)$. Treating it as a plain $\times$ after $\div$ gives the trap 145.

questions.q: What is the value of $\dfrac{5^{n+2} - 6 \cdot 5^{n+1}}{13 \cdot 5^{n} - 2 \cdot 5^{n+1}}$?
questions.solution: Take $5^n$ common from both: numerator $= 5^n(25 - 30) = -5 \cdot 5^n$, denominator $= 5^n(13 - 10) = 3 \cdot 5^n$. Value $= -\frac{5}{3}$.
questions.shortcut: Put $n = 0$: $\frac{25 - 30}{13 - 10} = -\frac{5}{3}$. Watch the signs — $13 + 10$ in the denominator gives the trap $-\frac{5}{23}$.

questions.q: In an examination, 35% of the candidates failed in Hindi, 25% failed in English and 10% failed in both subjects. If 300 candidates passed in both subjects, how many candidates appeared in the examination?
questions.solution: Failed in at least one subject $= 35 + 25 - 10 = 50\%$. Passed in both $= 100 - 50 = 50\%$. So $50\%$ of total $= 300 \Rightarrow$ total $= 600$.
questions.shortcut: Venn rule: $n(A \cup B) = A + B - \text{both}$. Forgetting to add back the 10% gives $40\%$ passing and the trap 750.

questions.q: Two numbers are respectively 30% and 50% more than a third number. The first number is what per cent of the second number?
questions.solution: Let the third number $= 100$. Then the first $= 130$ and the second $= 150$. Required $= \frac{130}{150} \times 100 = 86\frac{2}{3}\%$.

questions.q: The incomes of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 4 and their expenditures are in the ratio 3 : 2. If each of them saves ₹8,000, what is A's income?
questions.solution: Let incomes be $5x, 4x$ and expenditures $3y, 2y$. Then $5x - 3y = 8000$ and $4x - 2y = 8000$. From the second, $y = 2x - 4000$; substituting, $5x - 6x + 12000 = 8000 \Rightarrow x = 4000$. A's income $= 5x = ₹20{,}000$.
questions.shortcut: Equal savings: multiply to kill $y$ — $2(5x - 3y) - 3(4x - 2y) = 2(8000) - 3(8000) \Rightarrow -2x = -8000$, $x = 4000$. Check B: $16000 - 8000 = 8000$ saved.

questions.q: The average age of a family of 6 members is 25 years. If the youngest member is 7 years old, what was the average age of the family just before the birth of the youngest member?
questions.solution: Present total $= 6 \times 25 = 150$. Remove the youngest: $150 - 7 = 143$ for the other 5. Seven years ago each of these 5 was 7 years younger: $143 - 5 \times 7 = 108$. Average $= \frac{108}{5} = 21.6$ years.
questions.shortcut: Take away the child's age AND 7 years from each of the other 5: $\frac{150 - 7 - 35}{5} = 21.6$. Forgetting the 35 gives 28.6; dividing by 6 gives 18.

questions.q: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 8% per annum is ₹48. What is the sum?
questions.solution: For 2 years, $\text{CI} - \text{SI} = P\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)^2$. So $48 = P \times \frac{64}{10000} \Rightarrow P = \frac{48 \times 10000}{64} = ₹7{,}500$.
questions.shortcut: $\left(\frac{100}{R}\right)^2 = 12.5^2 = 156.25$; $48 \times 156.25 = 7500$. Using $\frac{100}{R}$ only once gives the trap 600.

questions.q: A shopkeeper buys pens at 15 for ₹100 and sells them at 12 for ₹100. What is his profit per cent?
questions.shortcut: Same money, different counts: profit $\% = \frac{\text{bought} - \text{sold}}{\text{sold}} \times 100 = \frac{3}{12} = 25\%$. Dividing by 15 instead gives the trap 20%.
questions.pattern: buy n sell m for same price

questions.q: The marked price of a cooler is ₹2,400. After two successive discounts, the first of 15% and the second of $x\%$, it is sold for ₹1,632. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: After the first discount: $2400 \times 0.85 = 2040$. Second discount $= \frac{2040 - 1632}{2040} \times 100 = \frac{408}{2040} \times 100 = 20\%$.
questions.shortcut: The single equivalent discount is $\frac{768}{2400} = 32\%$, but successive discounts do not subtract: $32 - 15 = 17$ is the trap. Work on the reduced price 2040.

questions.q: A is 60% more efficient than B. Working together, they can finish a piece of work in 20 days. In how many days can B alone finish the work?
questions.solution: Efficiency A : B $= 160 : 100 = 8 : 5$. Total work $= (8 + 5) \times 20 = 260$ units. B alone $= \frac{260}{5} = 52$ days.
questions.shortcut: Time $\propto \frac{1}{\text{efficiency}}$: B alone $= 20 \times \frac{8 + 5}{5} = 52$ days. $\frac{260}{8} = 32.5$ is A's time — a common mix-up.

questions.q: Two trains start at the same time from stations X and Y and move towards each other. After passing each other, the train from X takes 9 hours to reach Y and the train from Y takes 16 hours to reach X. If the speed of the train from X is 64 km/h, what is the speed of the train from Y?
questions.solution: Let them meet after $t$ hours. The part the X-train still has to cover ($64 \times 9$) was covered by the Y-train in $t$ hours, and vice versa: $S_Y t = 9 S_X$ and $S_X t = 16 S_Y$. Dividing, $\left(\frac{S_X}{S_Y}\right)^2 = \frac{16}{9}$, so $\frac{S_X}{S_Y} = \frac{4}{3}$ and $S_Y = \frac{3}{4} \times 64 = 48$ km/h.
questions.shortcut: $\frac{S_1}{S_2} = \sqrt{\frac{t_2}{t_1}}$ — the times go in reverse and under a square root: $\sqrt{\frac{16}{9}} = \frac{4}{3}$. Forgetting the root gives 36.

questions.q: If $x^2 - 7x + 1 = 0$, what is the value of $x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2}$?
questions.solution: Divide the equation by $x$: $x - 7 + \frac{1}{x} = 0 \Rightarrow x + \frac{1}{x} = 7$. Then $x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2} = 7^2 - 2 = 47$.
questions.shortcut: $x^2 - kx + 1 = 0$ means $x + \frac1x = k$; square and subtract 2. Adding 2 instead gives the trap 51.

questions.q: If $a + \frac{1}{a} = 3$, what is the value of $a^6 + \frac{1}{a^6}$?
questions.shortcut: Two routes, same answer: $a^3 + \frac{1}{a^3} = 27 - 9 = 18$, then square and subtract 2: $324 - 2 = 322$. Stopping at $7^3$ or $18^2$ gives the traps 343 and 324.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, the internal bisectors of $\angle B$ and $\angle C$ meet at $I$. If $\angle BIC = 118^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle A$?
questions.solution: For the incentre, $\angle BIC = 90^\circ + \frac{\angle A}{2}$. So $118 = 90 + \frac{A}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{A}{2} = 28^\circ \Rightarrow \angle A = 56^\circ$.
questions.shortcut: $\angle A = 2(\angle BIC - 90^\circ) = 2 \times 28 = 56^\circ$. Stopping at $28^\circ$ (forgetting to double) is the classic slip.

questions.q: The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is $1980^\circ$. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.solution: Sum of interior angles $= (n - 2) \times 180^\circ$. So $(n - 2) \times 180 = 1980 \Rightarrow n - 2 = 11 \Rightarrow n = 13$.
questions.shortcut: $1980 \div 180 = 11$, then add 2. Stopping at 11 is the trap.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, $AB = 10$ cm, $AC = 14$ cm and $BC = 16$ cm. If $AD$ is the median to $BC$, what is the length of $AD$?
questions.solution: Apollonius' theorem: $AB^2 + AC^2 = 2(AD^2 + BD^2)$ with $BD = 8$. So $100 + 196 = 2(AD^2 + 64) \Rightarrow AD^2 = 148 - 64 = 84 \Rightarrow AD = 2\sqrt{21}$ cm.
questions.shortcut: $AD^2 = \frac{AB^2 + AC^2}{2} - \left(\frac{BC}{2}\right)^2 = 148 - 64 = 84$. Forgetting to halve $296$ gives $2\sqrt{58}$; 12 is just the average of the two sides.

questions.q: From the top of a 45 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is $30^\circ$ and the angle of depression of the foot of the tower is $45^\circ$. What is the height of the tower?
questions.solution: Depression $45^\circ$ to the foot: horizontal distance $= 45$ m. Height of the tower above the building's roof $= 45 \tan 30^\circ = \frac{45}{\sqrt{3}} = 15\sqrt{3}$ m. Tower $= 45 + 15\sqrt{3} = 15(3 + \sqrt{3})$ m.
questions.shortcut: Tower $=$ building $+$ distance $\times \tan(\text{elevation})$ $= 45 + 45 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$. Using $\tan 60^\circ$ by mistake gives $45(1 + \sqrt{3})$.
questions.pattern: elevation and depression from a building

questions.q: What is the area of a triangle whose sides are 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm?
questions.solution: $s = \frac{13 + 14 + 15}{2} = 21$. Area $= \sqrt{21 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6} = \sqrt{7056} = 84$ cm².
questions.shortcut: 13-14-15 splits into two right triangles (5-12-13 and 9-12-15) on base 14 with height 12: $\frac{1}{2} \times 14 \times 12 = 84$. Treating it as right-angled ($\frac12 \times 13 \times 14 = 91$) is the trap.

questions.q: The base radius of a right circular cone is 21 cm and its curved surface area is 1914 cm². What is the volume of the cone? [Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$]
questions.solution: CSA $= \pi r l \Rightarrow 1914 = \frac{22}{7} \times 21 \times l = 66l \Rightarrow l = 29$ cm. Height $= \sqrt{29^2 - 21^2} = \sqrt{400} = 20$ cm. Volume $= \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21^2 \times 20 = 9240$ cm³.
questions.shortcut: 20-21-29 is a Pythagorean triplet — spot it and skip the square root. Using the slant height 29 as the height gives the trap 13398; dropping $\frac{1}{3}$ gives 27720.

questions.q: What is the value of $\sin^2 30^\circ + \cos^2 45^\circ + \tan^2 60^\circ$?
questions.shortcut: Square every value before adding. Using $\sin 30^\circ = \frac12$ unsquared gives 4; leaving $\tan 60^\circ = \sqrt3$ unsquared gives $\frac34 + \sqrt3$.

questions.q: If $\sec\theta + \tan\theta = 4$ and $\theta$ is acute, what is the value of $\cos\theta$?
questions.solution: Since $\sec^2\theta - \tan^2\theta = 1$, $(\sec\theta - \tan\theta) = \frac{1}{4}$. Adding the two equations: $2\sec\theta = 4 + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{17}{4} \Rightarrow \sec\theta = \frac{17}{8}$. So $\cos\theta = \frac{8}{17}$.
questions.shortcut: $\sec\theta = \frac{1}{2}\left(k + \frac{1}{k}\right)$ for $\sec\theta + \tan\theta = k$: $\frac{1}{2}\left(4 + \frac14\right) = \frac{17}{8}$, so $\cos\theta = \frac{8}{17}$. $\frac{15}{17}$ is $\sin\theta$ — read the question.

questions.q:
Find the mean of the following frequency distribution:

| $x$ | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $f$ | 3 | 5 | 9 | 2 | 1 |
questions.shortcut: Mean $= \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f}$ — divide by the total frequency 20, not by the 5 values (which gives 29.2). The plain average of $x$ (8) ignores the weights.

questions.q:
The table shows the number of laptops (in thousands) sold by five companies A, B, C, D and E in three years:

| Company | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 45 | 54 | 63 |
| B | 60 | 48 | 72 |
| C | 36 | 45 | 54 |
| D | 50 | 65 | 55 |
| E | 40 | 52 | 48 |

By what per cent did the sales of company B increase from 2023 to 2024?
questions.solution: B: 2023 $= 48$, 2024 $= 72$. Increase $= 24$. Per cent increase $= \frac{24}{48} \times 100 = 50\%$.
questions.shortcut: Divide the change by the OLD value (48). Dividing by the new value 72 gives the trap $33\frac13\%$; 20% compares 2024 with 2022.

questions.q:
The table shows the number of laptops (in thousands) sold by five companies A, B, C, D and E in three years:

| Company | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 45 | 54 | 63 |
| B | 60 | 48 | 72 |
| C | 36 | 45 | 54 |
| D | 50 | 65 | 55 |
| E | 40 | 52 | 48 |

The total sales of all five companies in 2023 is what per cent more than their total sales in 2022?
questions.shortcut: $\frac{33}{231} = \frac{1}{7} = 14\frac{2}{7}\%$ from the fraction table. Base is 2022 (the 'than' year); using 264 as the base gives $12\frac12\%$.

questions.q:
The table shows the number of laptops (in thousands) sold by five companies A, B, C, D and E in three years:

| Company | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 45 | 54 | 63 |
| B | 60 | 48 | 72 |
| C | 36 | 45 | 54 |
| D | 50 | 65 | 55 |
| E | 40 | 52 | 48 |

The average sales of companies A, B and C in 2024 is what per cent more than the average sales of companies D and E in 2022?
questions.shortcut: $\frac{63}{45} = \frac{7}{5} = 1.4 \Rightarrow 40\%$ more. Dividing 18 by 63 gives $28\frac47\%$ (wrong base); 18 is the raw difference, not a per cent.
